prompts.task: Produce a plan only for the Java Spring Boot service in ./service using eval/inputs/java-compatible-logging-candidates.json. Read the actual Maven/source fixture and the Java language guide; preserve its JDK, build, controller behavior, managed constraints and original logging sink. Treat the complete fictional candidate/configuration/lock matrix as a separate bounded source scenario, not a current published release or actual Maven/runtime receipt. Select the newest compatible agent and coherent bundled API/SDK/exporter/Logback bridge from those facts now, explain rejected candidates and protocol/public-appender support, and state whether an application API/SDK/appender dependency is needed for this auto-only request. No custom business spans or metrics are requested. Propose application of the exact checked agent artifact lock without a later floating-latest re-resolution; retain current Maven/BOM values. Plan the normal local native OTLP trace/metric/application-log baseline on the supplied nondefault receiver, with exact route/protocol/log field assertions, original console preservation and agent-owned shutdown. Assess each explicit opt-out/other-exporter and misconfiguration case according to the Java guide actual guard behavior, preserving unrelated targets/configuration and distinguishing blocked JVM launch from continuing trace/metric execution. Write only supplemental .observe/java-compatible-log-plan.md and .observe/java-compatible-log-plan.json, or concise linked equivalent details in those reports; do not generate canonical audit/selection/instrumentation/verification overlays or claim implementation/verification passed. Do not modify app code, manifests, locks, startup scripts, installed packages, shared sources or global configuration. Do not install/download dependencies, start services, invoke models/cloud/network, or run live instrumentation/verification. Supplied dates/hashes/versions are fictional source-plan provenance only; actual latest registry lookup, installed API support, app startup, native OTLP receiver records and cloud receipt are not proven. Use files/terminal only; do not open or control browsers, computer-use interfaces or other UI.

judge_inputs: Inspect actual service pom.xml, application.properties and TaskController.java separately from the complete fictional java-compatible-logging-candidates.json input. Read the loaded instrumentation Java guide, the source/plan instructions, generated supplemental Markdown/JSON, last_message.md, grade.json and the agent command trace. Equivalent grouped Markdown, JSON or linked evidence is valid. Grade the actual candidate, protocol, ownership and acceptance decisions, not particular headings or a prescribed JSON layout.

The supplied releases, artifacts, dependency graph, logging resolution, checksums and defaults are deliberately fictional but complete for this policy exercise. Require a concrete selection and justified rejections from that matrix. Do not require live release lookup, Maven resolution, SDK installation or real JAR inspection in this plan-only task. The actual application has no API-dependent custom telemetry or manual log provider; it does have an existing fixed SLF4J warning.

For a known generic-header or unsupported logs-protocol conflict, the current Java launcher removes only the added OTLP log member and starts Java with the original arguments, preserving other exporter members and trace/metric settings. Do not require those cases to block JVM startup. Configuration-file ownership and unsupported option syntax are separate preflight blockers. This task produces a plan, not current execution or receipts. Each item uses Rule, Example, Evidence and Insufficient evidence. Read all four together. Examples illustrate existing requirements; do not require their sample names, values or implementation unless the actual task/input selects them. Accept equivalent representative values and valid tests. Examples add no unselected work, and copying an example is not execution evidence. Explicit task requirements and supplied fixture values remain binding. Apply the item's role and applicability conditions to every section: audit plans required execution, while instrumentation and verification execute only within their existing authority. The Insufficient evidence examples are not exhaustive. They describe what does not by itself prove the rule. Missing proof alone is not_proven; an observed violation of an applicable requirement is fail. This includes false completion claims where the item treats them as violations. Optional or unselected work stays optional, and source-only evidence or an unsupported/unverified disposition remains valid wherever that item's rule allows it.
rubric:
Rule: Read the actual Java fixture and preserve JDK 21, the Maven/Spring Boot entrypoint, managed BOM/dependency properties and existing controller warning.
Example: The real controller uses SLF4J, while the supplied Logback configuration is fictional evidence for planning. Keep those sources distinct.
Evidence: Treat this as Java-agent auto-instrumentation without custom business spans. Identify the actual SLF4J source separately from the supplied fictional Logback/CONSOLE configuration; do not claim a real dependency:tree or runtime result. Use one agent-owned global provider and its bundled appender bridge. This auto-only application does not need an application API dependency, manual OpenTelemetryAppender, second SDK/provider or new application shutdown hook. Save source-based plans without changing application, build, lock, startup or global state, or inventing canonical findings.
Insufficient evidence: Claiming the fictional configuration was observed at runtime, or adding a second provider to this auto-only plan.

Rule: Choose the newest compatible coherent set from the complete fictional matrix.
Example: In this fictional matrix, agent 1.5.0 fits the supplied constraints while 1.6.0 does not; keep its bundled graph coherent.
Evidence: Agent 1.5.0 fits JDK 21, synthetic Logback 1.5.23/SLF4J 2.0.17 and the approved release constraint. Explain why 1.4.0 is older, 1.6.0 requires incompatible logging APIs, and 2.0.0 violates the JDK/release policy. Keep the selected bundled 9.1.0 API/SDK/exporter/appender graph together. Do not mix in API 9.2.0, which requires SDK 9.2.0, or force a framework, JDK or logging upgrade. Record the exact selection, rejected constraints and provenance of the supplied source records. These are fictional facts for this selection exercise, not actual latest releases or fixed versions to prescribe later.
Insufficient evidence: A generic promise to select compatible versions later, or selecting independently newest but incompatible components.

Rule: Use the selected public agent's actual transport and appender capabilities, not a guessed version-number threshold.
Example: The selected fictional agent defaults to grpc but supports the desired HTTP/protobuf route, so the plan must configure that route explicitly.
Evidence: The fictional selected agent defaults to grpc but explicitly supports http/protobuf and agent-owned native LogRecord export, so specify the desired local HTTP/protobuf configuration. Plan future application of the exact checked 1.5.0 coordinate/digest and bundled graph through the supplied external-agent lock. Preserve existing Maven-managed constraints and add no unnecessary application telemetry dependency. Do not download a floating latest release or resolve a mutable tag again after preflight; fictional latest drift to incompatible 2.1.0 cannot replace the checked graph. Real artifact/API installation has not run and is not proved by fictional metadata or a checksum.
Insufficient evidence: Guessing protocol support from a version label, re-resolving latest after preflight, or treating a fictional checksum as installation proof.

Rule: Plan the normal local OTLP logging path with OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp when there is no opt-out, alongside native traces and metrics.
Example: The future native warning must arrive on the supplied nondefault logs route and join the actual POST/tasks span.
Evidence: Use the supplied nondefault HTTP receiver on port 55318, explicit supported protocol, separate /v1/traces, /v1/metrics and /v1/logs routes, and the complete signal-specific logs endpoint. Use exactly one agent-owned Logback bridge/provider/export path, preserving CONSOLE level, formatter and additivity. Future execution must capture one real-application warning LogRecord with Body runtime request completed, WARN text/severity 13, TaskController logger/scope, and java-springboot-basic/local Resource identity shared with traces/metrics. In-span IDs must join an actual received POST/tasks span; the planned outside-span record must not have invented IDs. Configuration, source, SDK spans or console correlation alone do not prove native log receipt. Execution and route acceptance remain unproven in this plan.
Insufficient evidence: Console correlation, SDK span output or a configuration file without the planned real native LogRecord assertions.

Rule: Plan explicit opt-outs separately.
Example: An explicit JVM none selection overrides environment otlp; a separate isolated log conflict must preserve the original native and other-signal paths.
Evidence: Effective JVM -Dotel.logs.exporter=none must override environment otlp. An explicit console exporter must not add another local pipeline, SDK/provider/appender or change the original sink. Zero-OTLP-log checks do not prove the normal default path. For generic cloud headers or unsupported http/json, follow the current guard: remove only the added OTLP log member for that invocation, preserve other exporter members and original JVM arguments, and plan independent trace/metric and native-sink continuity checks. This is isolated log-conflict handling, not a persisted normal none default or proof of executed startup. Propose moving generic cloud credentials to trace/metric-specific settings only through reviewed preflight configuration. Do not mutate credentials at runtime/globally, use wildcard MDC, route logs to cloud, or invent receipts.
Insufficient evidence: Treating a conflict-only none guard as the persisted normal profile, or changing credentials at runtime.

Rule: Give a concrete future test plan for the application's existing warning: exactly one received native LogRecord and one original console record, matching Body, severity, logger, Resource and correlation, plus an outside-span ID-absence check.
Example: The plan must distinguish one native received warning plus one original console record from a duplicate collection path.
Evidence: Include normal native trace/metric receipt and agent-owned JVM shutdown delivery without new application hooks or providers. In both reports, distinguish fictional API/lock/configuration support, actual source inspection and unexecuted application/runtime/receiver/cloud checks. Keep explicit opt-out and isolated log-misconfiguration probes separate from normal acceptance. Do not describe synthetic candidates, defaults, hashes, plan text or invented IDs as installed artifacts, live telemetry, a fresh registry lookup or completed instrumentation.
Insufficient evidence: Passing plan prose or fictional metadata presented as completed runtime acceptance.
